;Armed conflicts and attacks
*The [[United Nations]] human rights office says that [[Myanmar]] has been carrying out daily airstrikes in [[Rakhine State|Rakhine]] and [[Chin State|Chin]] states and that at least 32 civilians (mostly women and children) have been killed since March 23. The [[Arakan Army (Kachin State)|Arakan Army]] unilaterally declared a month-long ceasefire to fight the [[COVID-19]] pandemic, but the military rejected the ceasefire saying a previous ceasefire had not been respected by the insurgents. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-rakhine-un/u-n-says-at-least-32-people-mostly-women-and-children-killed-as-insurgents-myanmar-military-clash-idUSKBN21Z1DJ (Reuters)]
*[[Moro conflict]]
**[[Abu Sayyaf]] militants ambush and kill 11 [[Philippine Army]] troops and wound 14 others in the southern [[Sulu Province]], according to [[general officer]] [[Cirilito Sobejana]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/militants-kill-11-philippine-troops-wound-14 (''The Straits Times'')]

;Business and economy
*The [[China Securities Regulatory Commission]] has approved a transaction in which Switzerland's [[Credit Suisse]] will take a majority interest in a China securities firm. Credit Suisse will thus be the first foreign bank to own a majority of such a company since the easing of rules about foreign ownership in 2018. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-credit-suisse-gp-china/credit-suisse-gets-approval-to-take-majority-stake-in-china-jv-idUSKBN21Z1V7 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****Former [[England national football team|England]] international and [[Leeds United F.C.]] footballer [[Norman Hunter (footballer)|Norman Hunter]] dies from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52246007 (BBC News)]
****The [[Department of Health and Social Care]] reports 5,599 new confirmed cases and 847 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the UK's death toll to 14,576 and 108,692 total cases. [https://www.rte.ie/news/2020/0417/1132174-uk-figures-covid19/ (RTÉ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Syria]]
****The Kurdish-controlled area of [[Syria]] confirms the first death from COVID-19 in [[Qamishli]]; that of a 53-year-old man who tested positive postmortem. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-syria-northeast/syrias-northeast-confirms-first-death-from-coronavirus-statement-idUSKBN21Z2SX (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] revises the coronavirus death toll upward in [[Wuhan]], where the virus originated, adding 1,290 more fatalities to bring the country's reported deaths from COVID-19 to 4,632. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-52321529 (BBC News)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/17/coronavirus-live-updates-singapore-new-record-high-china-numbers.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****[[Dubai]] extends their 24-hour curfew by one week. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-emirates/dubai-extends-24-hour-coronavirus-curfew-by-one-week-idUSL8N2C550G (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****[[Nigeria]]n [[Chief of Staff to the President (Nigeria)|Chief of Staff to the President]] [[Abba Kyari (politician)|Abba Kyari]] dies from COVID-19 in [[Lagos]]. Kyari is the highest profile person to die from the virus in Nigeria so far. The [[Nigeria Centre for Disease Control]] reports 493 total cases and 17 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-nigeria/nigerian-presidents-chief-of-staff-dies-from-coronavirus-presidency-spokesman-idUSKBN220001?il=0 (Reuters)]
